decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “paste a link… click ‘Fetch details’… click Save bookmark”; round 3 client: “this quick-save flow works for me.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review decision conforms to saving a bookmark by URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker specifies an auto-filled “title” and “a description shown for context,” without favicon or preview-image collection; round 3 client approves the flow without mentioning those missing fields.
decisions.note: Prototype metadata collection omits two required metadata fields. The client does not express the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “auto-filled title as editable after fetching (with a description shown for context)”; round 3 client: “Editing the fetched title is useful.”
decisions.note: Prototype review establishes title editing but only displays the description and does not establish description editing before or after save.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker asks the client to “add a tag or two” and describes removable tag chips; round 3 client says the chips feel natural.
decisions.note: Prototype supports assigning one or more tags.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker defines tag entry as “type one and press Enter”; round 9 maker declares the summarized features to be the “full scope,” still mentioning only optional tags. Round 9 client gives bare scope approval.
decisions.note: By the specification gate, existing-tag autocomplete is outside the declared scope. Neither approval identifies that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents the note as “an optional free-text line”; round 3 client calls it “the right amount of effort.” Round 9 full scope still specifies only a “short note.”
decisions.note: The scoped note is plain short text rather than a Markdown note rendered on viewing; the client does not state or accept that difference explicitly.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker says search matches “title, its note, its link, and its tags”; round 4 client endorses broad search but mentions remembering a note rather than a title.
decisions.note: Prototype search omits description from the required full-text fields. The client does not surface the omission.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents word search plus tags as a separate “click-to-filter” mechanism; round 4 client approves keeping clickable filters alongside search. Round 9 declares this the full scope.
decisions.note: The specified search/filter design does not include #tag syntax, and the client never expresses that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: click a tag chip “to filter to just those bookmarks”; round 4 client: “Keeping clickable tag filters alongside search is useful.”
decisions.note: Prototype review conforms to filtering by a selected tag.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker specifies narrowing by typing “a word.” Round 9 maker declares simple broad search and clickable tag filters to be the “full scope” and says nothing else will be added; round 9 client approves that scope.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, case-insensitive semantics, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, and quoted exact phrases are omitted from the exhaustive search scope. The client gives only bare approval.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents Read later as a reversible toggle with a separate tab; round 5 client says it “should be a reversible choice.”
decisions.note: Prototype behavior is functionally equivalent to marking unread, viewing unread separately, and marking read to remove it.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker says Archive removes links from All and Read later, keeps them in an Archive tab, and offers “Restore to All”; round 5 client explicitly wants them hidden, searchable, and restorable there.
decisions.note: Archive is separate, reversible, and excluded from ordinary views, conforming to the archive-related behavior presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker presents a card with unusually long title, note, and many tags for a readability check; round 7 client: “The long content remains readable enough.”
decisions.note: This recorded prototype decision conforms to the readability aspect of the list requirement; required field exposure is assessed separately at the exhaustive scope gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker says failed auto-fill does not block saving and lets the user “type your own title and save anyway”; round 7 client confirms that expectation.
decisions.note: The failure-path decision preserves URL saving and permits pre-save editing rather than contradicting those requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker proposes refusing “a completely invalid link”; round 7 client says it “should be refused.”
decisions.note: Rejecting a non-URL conforms to the required URL constraint.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker offers warning about a duplicate and “let you decide,” or saving it again; round 7 client responds: “warn me and guide me to edit the existing bookmark rather than creating another copy.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review correction supplies the reference-conforming convergence behavior because neither offered behavior fully required editing the existing item.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker presents a warning, an “Edit the saved bookmark” action, and “no second copy”; round 8 client confirms it prevents a copy and opens the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate flow conforms after the earlier correction.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker defines always-available editing as revising “a title, note, or tags”; round 8 client says to keep it for revising “the title, note, or tags later.”
decisions.note: The edit decision omits URL and description editing, including post-save description editing. The client repeats the limited field set without identifying the missing required fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker calls the listed features the “full scope” and includes archive/restore but no delete or permanent-removal behavior; round 9 client: “build the real application with that scope.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, deletion and the required archive-versus-permanent-delete distinction are omitted. Bare approval does not capture the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker’s exhaustive scope lists search, filters, state tabs, duplicate handling, and editing, but no requirement to expose description/favicon on every item or make item selection open the original URL; round 9 client gives bare approval.
decisions.note: The declared full scope omits required list-field exposure and original-URL navigation.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker declares the summarized features to be the “full scope,” with no multi-selection, bulk actions, or apply-to-current-filter operation; round 9 client approves it.
decisions.note: Bulk selection and both selected-item and whole-filter bulk actions are outside the approved specification, without the client expressing the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 exhaustive scope contains no sorting control or sort key; round 9 client approves that scope.
decisions.note: List sorting is omitted at the specification gate and passes without corrective response.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker’s “full scope” contains neither local HTML/PDF snapshots nor Internet Archive snapshots; round 9 client approves the scope.
decisions.note: Both snapshot capabilities are excluded from the exhaustive scope without observable client recognition.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 full scope includes transient search and tag filtering but no saved filter/bundle capability; round 9 client approves.
decisions.note: Reusable bundles of search and included/excluded tags are omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker’s exhaustive scope contains no Netscape HTML import or export; round 9 client approves it.
decisions.note: Import and export are omitted without a corrective or explicitly accepting statement from the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 full scope contains no personal default-sort, displayed-items, or font-size settings; round 9 client approves it.
decisions.note: Personal display settings are outside the exhaustive scope, and the client does not identify the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports the real application supports “paste a link” and that the quick-save usage flow passes; round 10 client accepts the application.
decisions.note: Implementation-review presentation conforms to URL-based saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports automatic “details” but clarifies only that the exact “title/description depends on the site”; favicon and preview-image collection are not part of the implementation report. Round 10 client gives blanket acceptance.
decisions.note: Implementation review repeats the metadata-field divergence; the client does not express it.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports an Edit option on every entry, inheriting the approved round 8 field set of title, note, and tags; round 10 client gives blanket acceptance.
decisions.note: The delivered edit behavior still lacks URL and description editing. Final approval does not identify that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports that quick-save can “add tags” and that the usage flow passes; round 10 client accepts.
decisions.note: Delivered tag assignment conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports adding tags but no existing-tag autocomplete, consistent with the approved manual-chip scope; round 10 client gives blanket acceptance.
decisions.note: Implementation review retains the omitted autocomplete behavior without client expression.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports adding “a note,” consistent with the scoped short free-text note, and does not report Markdown rendering; round 10 client gives blanket acceptance.
decisions.note: The delivered note behavior remains below the Markdown-note requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker says implemented search runs “across title, note, link and tags”; description remains absent. Round 10 client accepts the application.
decisions.note: Implementation review explicitly confirms the incomplete full-text field set.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports tag filtering as a verified flow; round 10 client accepts.
decisions.note: Delivered tag filtering conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 implementation report describes search across fixed fields and separate tag filtering, with no case-insensitivity guarantee, #tag syntax, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, or exact-phrase syntax; round 10 client gives blanket acceptance.
decisions.note: The delivered search presentation retains the specification-gate omissions. Final approval does not explicitly identify or accept any of them.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports the “reversible Read later list” as a passing flow; round 10 client accepts.
decisions.note: Implementation-review behavior conforms to unread/read-later management.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports archiving “out of the way, still searchable and restorable” as a passing flow; round 10 client accepts.
decisions.note: The delivered archive behavior itself conforms; permanent deletion remains a separately recorded scope divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker reports a passing “Duplicate warning that guides you to edit the existing bookmark”; round 10 client accepts.
decisions.note: Final implementation presentation conforms to duplicate convergence.
